title: Genius idea to handle the risk of your game being copied and put on Roblox
author: Codingology
selftext:
If your game trailer got more than 10 likes there’s already a chance someone might vibecode it in Roblox and add ton of microtransactions.

Since this phenomena has gotten insanely viral, it’s safe for you to assume that your game IS going to be copied, if you believe it’s a good game at least.

How to combat this? 

Simply be you the guy who creates the Roblox slop version of your own game.  
When you are ready to deploy the official game you should already have done the slop one on Roblox studio, and release the Roblox version shortly after announcing to the public the original game.

You’re welcome

comments.author: Ravesoull
comments.body: Nope, I don't even want to touch the shit named Roblox.

replies.author: fungus_is_amungus
replies.body: Real. The net code is so fucking bad in Roblox. I genuinely don't understand how anyone plays anything in it.the desync is crazy.

replies.author: fungus_is_amungus
replies.body: Idk man. When I was a kid I played either games that were singplayer or didn't require good connection. The blood of my 10 yo self was boiling when playing cs1.6 on 200 ping.

replies.author: jackadgery85
replies.body:
I played cs 1.6 on 180+ permanently, and maintain it's what made me great at fps games.

However i have worked in school aged care for a decade now, and can tell you roblox is where 90% of them are

replies.author: fungus_is_amungus
replies.body:
Damn, you were one patient kid lol. 

Kinda forgot that kids just play whatever is cheaper(or free I guess) and whatever their friends play. I forgot I played on a cracked 1.6 version lmao

replies.author: jackadgery85
replies.body: 100% it's whatever their friends are playing, or whatever the most trending youtuber that their peers are all watching is playing

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body:
The target audience on Roblox isn't remotely my own target audience. If some kid wants to have at it, I wish him all the best.

But so far my shitty youtube trailer only got 80 views and 4 likes so I'm all good anyway.

replies.author: Codingology
replies.body: Yea makes sense. I made this post for people who have a very interesting and innovative concept for a game. I’ve seen often straight adults saying “seems fun, gonna wait to play it for free on Roblox”

comments.author: bob_at
comments.body: What’s your prompt for this? Slop my game into roblox. Make no mistakes?

replies.author: Codingology
replies.body:
Ahaha usually Roblox servers are far more permessive to mistakes, bugs and overall lack of effort since the main target are children.   
Just say to the agent to replicate as best as possible your game using Lua and then make the final touches and add dumb microtransactions

replies.author: Domy9
replies.body: It doesn't matter if it's shit, whoever would copy it would also make it low effort so they just check if a copy already exists, not that if a *good* copy exists

comments.author: ImCallingYouOutOnBS
comments.body: I could've sworn I just watched a video about a game studio doing this with one of their releases, and the Roblox version actually made more money. Its insane

comments.author: tractiv
comments.body: Only problem could be a bigger creator stealing your idea, since they have a community on Roblox they get a ton of players from the get go and your Roblox version of game could go unnoticed for the most part. This is a general problem on Roblox, even with games that are Roblox exclusive. If you have a good idea it’s likely that a bigger creator will steal it

If someone creates a poor version of my game on roblox it will probably function as a demo and drive customers to the real game.

replies.author: jawni
replies.body: If you mean detailed as in the graphics, you should check out what Roblox games can look like in 2026.

comments.body: Honestly, thank you. I'm gonna do this. Quite frankly, i needed a break from my game. Might be fun to tackle a roblox clone of my game.
